newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany seeks more Iranians for dissident killings.
newsitem.headline: Germany seeks more Iranians for dissident killings.

text.p: German prosecutors said on Thursday they had issued arrest warrants for three Iranian secret service officials suspected of taking part in the 1992 assassination of Kurdish dissidents in Berlin.

They said an arrest warrant issued last year against Iranian Intelligence Minister Ali Fallahiyan on suspicion of ordering the attack would remain in force but no other Iranian leaders would be investigated over the attack.

Two of the suspects were believed to have helped prepare the attack, the third to have led the gang which carried it out. Last month a Berlin court convicted one Iranian and three Lebanese for carryinh out the attack.

The court concluded that Iranian political leaders, who sat on a secret "special operations committee", ordered the killing of four Kurdish exiles in a Berlin restaurant. It said these included Iran's president and its supreme religious leader.
The Federal Prosecutor's Office said it was not clear to what extent these leaders enjoyed immunity under international law.

"There is no basis for investigating the precise circumstances of the committee's decision or to prove the concrete participation of the committee members, apart from Fallahiyan," it said in a statement."In this situation it is not in the public interest to start an investigation against the committee members."
